answer:
## HYPOTHESIS (final answer)

**The gardening pathway has no single prevalence style in this region: it switches style across the boundary between intensively human-held ground (Urban, Croplands) and low-elevation, moist, disturbed ground (Wetlands, Coastal, and less strongly Riparian) — and the switch is in *dominance*, not in *frequency*, which is why any one metric gives a contradictory answer.**

Garden-introduced species are encountered equally often in the city and in the wetlands — plots containing ≥1 gardening species: Urban 0.477 (31/65) vs Wetlands+Coastal 0.478 (32/67), OR 1.00, Fisher p = 1.0 — yet among the non-native species actually present, gardening supplies 55% of records in Wetlands (29/52) and 54% in Coastal (23/43) but only 30% in Urban (45/151) and 19% in Croplands (20/108), against a regional 35% (169/481). Labels: Wetlands and Coastal = **frequent-and-co-dominant** (Holm p vs leave-one-out share 0.005 and 0.061; gardening not outnumbered by unintentional, p = 0.87 and 0.78); Urban and Croplands = **frequent-but-subordinate** (gardening:unintentional 0.43 and 0.24, p = 7e-07 and 1e-10); Riparian = **frequent-and-proportional** (occupancy 0.361, share 0.365).

The context in which this habitat contrast exists is **low urban cover and low elevation**. Stratifying invaded plots by 1000 m urban cover, the azonal-vs-urbanised gardening share OR is 14.4 [2.68, 77.8] where urban cover < 0.02, 6.18 [2.74, 13.9] at 0.02–0.20, and collapses to 1.43 [0.86, 2.36], p = 0.20 where urban cover > 0.20; it likewise shrinks 7.35 → 4.07 → 1.81 as plot invader richness rises. Inside the urbanisation saturation zone habitat identity stops mattering, because unintentional (seed-contaminant/trade) introductions swamp the gardening signal. Pooling, the azonal dominance OR is 2.50 [1.67, 3.72] (p = 8e-06), 2.90 [2.06, 4.09] in a quasi-binomial model conditioned on `urban.2009.50m`, elevation and `distance.road`, 2.47–2.81 within CMH strata of urban cover, elevation and plot richness (all p < 1e-05), and 2.88 after adding 1956 cropland cover. Elevation is the strongest single covariate on frequency (OR 0.27 [0.19, 0.40] per SD; occupancy 0.360 → 0.167 → 0.028 across tertiles); urban cover moves frequency (occupancy 0.025 → 0.420 across 1000 m classes) but leaves share flat (0.31–0.37); `distance.stream` is irrelevant (rho = 0.031, p = 0.43), so the water axis acts through habitat membership, not proximity. Habitat and context are independently informative: adding habitat to a context-only model gives LR chi2 = 51.5, df = 2, p = 6.6e-12; adding context to a habitat model gives p = 3.2e-08.

**Metric dependence is part of the answer.** Frequency- and dominance-based rankings of the ten habitats are statistically unrelated (Spearman rho = 0.079, p = 0.82); restricted to invaded plots they agree (rho = 0.985), so the disagreement is generated by how many uninvaded plots each habitat contributes. Reading frequency alone would class Urban with Wetlands; reading share alone would rank Broad-leaved forests first (share 1.00 on 3 invaded plots and 4 records) — a vanishing-denominator artefact.

**Bounds.** Rock outcrops (1 invaded plot, 1 record) and Scrublands (3, 5) are **no evidence of gardening / undetermined**, never demonstrated absence; Broad-leaved forests (3, 4), Coniferous forests (5, 8) and Meadows (5, 13) are "garden-origin relics recorded where little else establishes", a low-n caution rather than a style.

Background, one sentence: region-wide gardening is the dominant introduction pathway (611/1046 records, rising 18 → 397 across periods), but that table has no habitat axis and was not combined with the plot data.

## Workflow executed
1. Granularity established in the approved inspection: `invaded_niche_pathways.csv` = 632 plots (unique coordinates) with per-plot pathway richness; `invasion_success_pathways.csv` = 81 species, no habitat identity; temporal table = period × pathway; tree unused.
2. Prevalence-style table per habitat: occupancy P(n.gard>0) with Wilson CI, dominance share with leave-one-out Holm binomial test, within-habitat gardening-vs-unintentional binomial test, intensity per occupied plot, reliability gate (≥15 occurrences and ≥15 invaded plots).
3. Dual weighting (plot-level vs occurrence-weighted, plus invaded-plot-conditional) so weighting cannot flip the story.
4. Habitat(10) × pathway(3) tested by permutation Fisher–Freeman–Halton (B = 5000, p = 0.0002, V = 0.28; plain chi-square withheld — 17/30 expected cells < 5, min 0.05); collapsed 2×2 and 3×2 contrasts with Fisher OR + CI + Cramér's V, reported both occurrence- and plot-weighted.
5. Firth penalised logistic (own implementation, validated exactly on the analytic 0/10 separation case and against MLE on clean data) for occupancy; nested LR comparisons habitat vs context; invaded-plot-only models; quasi-binomial dominance model; Poisson and NB2 count check; CMH stratified tests plus stratum-specific ORs; threshold and habitat-grouping sensitivity analyses.
6. Species-level `habitat.range ~ pathway` reported strictly as corroboration, with and without the 4 duplicated rows.

## Evidence
Habitat table (occupancy | share | invaded plots | style): Wetlands 0.500 | 0.558 | 21 | frequent-and-co-dominant; Urban 0.477 | 0.298 | 54 | frequent-but-subordinate; Coastal 0.448 | 0.535 | 16 | frequent-and-co-dominant; Riparian 0.361 | 0.365 | 32 | frequent-and-proportional; Croplands 0.207 | 0.185 | 51 | frequent-but-subordinate; Meadows 0.077 | 0.308 | 5; Coniferous forests 0.065 | 0.875 | 5; Broad-leaved forests 0.044 | 1.000 | 3; Scrublands 0.019 | 0.400 | 3; Rock outcrops 0.000 | 0.000 | 1 (last five undetermined). Intensity per occupied plot 1.00–1.77 (no habitat differences in how many garden species a colonised plot holds). Occupancy ORs: azonal vs terrestrial-natural 18.75 [9.73, 36.12] (p = 1.6e-23); urbanised vs rest 2.85 [1.86, 4.35]. Count model fits cleanly (Poisson dispersion 1.12, NB2 converged, azonal IRR 1.71–1.72, elevation IRR 0.48–0.49) but is dominated by 515/632 zeros, so it only echoes the frequency axis. Species-level corroboration: habitat.range 1.95 (Gardening) vs 2.77 (Unintentional), one-sided MWU p = 0.042, weakening to p = 0.082 excluding duplicates.

## Limitations
All models exploratory; unpenalised habitat logistic is quasi-separated (singular Hessian), so Firth was required and penalised LR tests are approximate. Habitat is partly defined by the land cover regressed on (mean 50 m urban cover 0.689 Urban vs 0.006 Scrublands), so the Urban row is context-confirming, not independent. No species-per-plot identity, so we cannot separate "garden species are poor colonisers" from "garden records concentrate where ornamentals are planted"; the azonal grouping is ecological post hoc though the contrast is stable under three alternative assignments (OR 2.50–3.61). Occurrence-level tests treat records within a plot as independent (plot-weighted versions reported alongside; CMH stratified by plot richness). Cross-table totals left unreconciled (481 plot-level vs 472 species-level, ~2%).

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway shows different prevalence styles across habitat types specifically in the low-urban-cover, low-elevation part of the landscape: in moist, disturbed azonal habitats (Wetlands and Coastal, with Riparian intermediate) gardening is frequent AND co-dominant (occupancy 0.45-0.50; gardening supplies 54-56% of pathway-coded invader records, Holm p=0.005/0.061 vs the regional 35%), whereas in intensively human-held Urban and Croplands plots it is frequent but subordinate (equally often encountered - Urban 0.477 vs Wetlands+Coastal 0.478, OR 1.00 - yet only 19-30% of records, outnumbered by unintentional introductions 0.24-0.43:1, p<=7e-07). The contrast is not a richness or detectability artefact (invaded-plot richness p=0.089) and survives conditioning on urban cover, elevation, road proximity, historical cropland and CMH stratification (pooled dominance OR 2.50 [1.67,3.72]; adjusted 2.90 [2.06,4.09]), but it exists only outside the urbanisation saturation zone: the OR is 14.4 where 1000 m urban cover <0.02 and 1.43 (p=0.20) where it exceeds 0.20, and it decays from 7.35 to 1.81 as plot invader richness rises, because heavy unintentional introduction pressure homogenises pathway composition. In the dry upland habitats (Rock outcrops, Scrublands, both forest types, Meadows) there is too little gardening signal to assign any style (1-5 invaded plots, 1-13 records): no evidence of gardening, not demonstrated absence. Because frequency and dominance rank the ten habitats almost independently (Spearman rho=0.079, p=0.83; rho=0.985 restricted to invaded plots), the conclusion depends on using both metrics: frequency alone would class Urban with Wetlands, while share alone would put Broad-leaved forests first on 4 records.
payload.workflow: Plot-level pathway-richness data only (632 plots; species-level table used solely as corroboration; temporal table cited as background; tree unused). (1) Prevalence-style table per habitat: frequency = occupancy P(n.gard>0) with Wilson CI; dominance = n.gard/n.total with Holm-adjusted leave-one-out binomial test plus within-habitat gardening-vs-unintentional binomial test; intensity = mean n.gard per occupied plot; reliability gate >=15 occurrences and >=15 invaded plots; labels frequent-and-co-dominant / frequent-but-subordinate / frequent-and-proportional / rare-but-exclusive / absent-or-undetermined. (2) Plot-weighted and occurrence-weighted versions of every habitat table. (3) Permutation Fisher-Freeman-Halton for habitat(10)xpathway(3) and habitat(3)xpathway(2) (plain chi-square not used; 17/30 expected cells <5); collapsed Fisher exact contrasts with OR, 95% CI, Cramer V, both weightings. (4) Firth penalised logistic for occupancy (own implementation, validated) with nested LR tests of habitat vs context (urban cover 50 m/1000 m, elevation, log distance to road, land-cover change, 1956 cropland), invaded-plot-only models, quasi-binomial dominance model on invaded plots, Poisson/NB2 count check, CMH stratified tests and stratum-specific ORs, sensitivity to style thresholds and to habitat grouping. (5) Species-level habitat.range ~ pathway with and without duplicated rows, labelled corroboration only.
key_findings: Frequency and dominance metrics rank habitats almost independently (Spearman rho=0.079, p=0.83), agreeing only when restricted to invaded plots (rho=0.985)
Urban vs Wetlands+Coastal: identical occupancy (0.477 vs 0.478, OR 1.00, p=1) but opposite dominance (0.298 vs 0.547, OR 0.35 [0.21,0.60], p=1.6e-4)
Azonal-semi-aquatic vs urbanised-cultivated dominance OR 2.50 [1.67,3.72] (p=8.2e-6); 2.90 [2.06,4.09] adjusted for urban cover, elevation, road distance; 2.47-2.81 within CMH strata
Style gap vanishes above 20% urban cover (OR 1.43, p=0.20) and shrinks with plot invader richness (7.35 -> 4.07 -> 1.81): urbanisation saturation homogenises pathway composition
Habitat survives conditioning on context: LR chi2=51.5 df=2 p=6.6e-12 (groups), 70.0 df=9 p=1.5e-11 (10 habitats); context also adds to habitat (p=3.2e-8)

Elevation strongest covariate on frequency (OR 0.27 per SD; occupancy 0.360->0.167->0.028); urban cover shifts frequency (0.025->0.42) but not share (0.31-0.37); distance to stream irrelevant (rho=0.031, p=0.43)

Habitat is partly defined by the land cover regressed on (mean 50 m urban cover 0.689 Urban vs 0.006 Scrublands), so the Urban row is context-confirming, not independent evidence
No species-by-plot identity: cannot separate poor colonisation by garden species from concentration of records near ornamental plantings
Azonal habitat grouping is ecological but post hoc; stable under three alternative assignments (dominance OR 2.50-3.61)
